subject: 0E46A9D425ED4F89AB54563B472E6EF6
introduction: The guide asks what kind of power a Messenger of God has. Its readings answer in a sequence: a young man without rank overturns an ancient law and remakes a people’s morals; the evidence is that change, more than any wonder; his word creates; he does what he wills and is not to be asked why; and, the claim the guide returns to most, he prevails from inside a prison. The Gospels already hold most of this: authority “not as the scribes”, the world turned upside down, miracles that did not persuade and a town where none could be done, “all power is given unto me”, and a conversation with a governor about where power comes from. The Qur’an points to its own verses when signs are demanded. The questions are sharp ones. Abraham asked the Judge of all the earth whether he would do right, and Socrates whether the holy is holy because it is loved; the priests at the cross and Dostoevsky’s Inquisitor think real power would come down and rule; Machiavelli counts unarmed prophets among the destroyed; Paine doubts that any proof reaches the second hearer.
questions: Jesus “could there do no mighty work” in his own country, and many who saw miracles did not believe. Why do readings 29, 30 and 42 to 46 prefer the transformation of people to wonders as evidence?
“Is it not enough for them that We have sent down unto thee the Scripture?” What does it mean to offer the verses themselves as proof, and how would Paine’s objection be met?
“Why and wherefore do not apply to His ways” (179). Abraham asked “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?” Is Abraham’s question excluded by the reading, or is it another thing?

The priests say, “let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe”. What idea of power do they share with the Grand Inquisitor and with Machiavelli, and what idea do readings 191 to 216 put in its place?
“The word of God is not bound.” What exactly prevailed from the prison, according to the readings, and by what means?
The last readings speak of power given to those who serve. How is that power like and unlike the power described in the rest of the guide?

outside.why: “This young Man, Christ, through an extraordinary power” set aside an ancient law. The people were astonished at his doctrine: for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
The reading says he abrogated the Mosaic Law. Jesus says: think not that I am come to destroy the law; I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil. How are both statements to be held?
The Manifestations have always appeared “destitute of all earthly dominion”. He hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him.
Zechariah’s picture of the promised king has the same poverty in it: thy King cometh unto thee, lowly, and riding upon an ass.
In the wilderness Jesus is offered all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, and refuses. The absence of dominion is chosen. What kind of power is left?
As the visible sun develops all earthly things. Unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings.
When Christ appeared, minds and customs were overturned. The complaint at Thessalonica: these that have turned the world upside down are come hither also.
The opposition was not trivial. God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty.
He arose with such power as “to shake the foundations” of laws and customs. Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain.
The proof offered is the change in persons and peoples. Saul, breathing out threatenings, is thrown down on the Damascus road by a light from heaven.
A story of a man changed. Zacchaeus stood, and said: the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
“Let us speak a little of proofs.” Believe me that I am in the Father: or else believe me for the very works’ sake.
Should the miracles be taken literally? Maimonides held that Israel did not believe in Moses because of the wonders he performed, for belief that rests on wonders is always open to doubt.
Wonders appeared from him continually. John records the result in his own story: though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him.
In his own country he could there do no mighty work, and he marvelled because of their unbelief. If power waits on the capacity of those who receive it, what does that say about miracle as proof?
“Ask whatsoever ye please.” The Qur’an records the demand and the reply: portents are with God only, and I am but a plain warner.
He read none of their books, yet answers whatever is asked. How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?
“The Breath of God awakened Him and commanded Him.” The spirit entered into me when he spake unto me, and set me upon my feet.
The mysteries of days to come were revealed to the Prophets. Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.
He “sent down the verses … and hath made them a proof”. The Qur’an’s answer to those who want signs: is it not enough for them that We have sent down unto thee the Scripture which is read unto them?
The proof is perfected in the verses themselves. If ye are in doubt concerning that which We reveal, then produce a surah of the like thereof.

“His proof more perfect than all that exists.” Paine: a revelation is revelation to the first person only; to every other it is hearsay, and I am not obliged to believe it. What proof reaches the second person?
The reality of prophethood, the Word of God, “has neither beginning nor end”. In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God.
The Word is sanctified beyond time. Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.
The Perfect Man is the expression of the Creator’s complete thought. Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.
The tree of life is the station of the Word. Wisdom in Proverbs: the Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way; I was daily his delight.
“That Perfect Word, that Manifest Book.” The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory.
They come to purify man of his animal nature. That by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature.
“Had God willed … He would have manifested a thousand times” such signs. Asked for a house of gold or an ascent to heaven, the Prophet is to say: am I aught save a mortal messenger?
Every letter has power “to bring into existence a new creation”. By the word of the Lord were the heavens made: he spake, and it was done.
The first speech in Genesis is of this kind: God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
He could make a speck of dust generate suns. When He decreeth a thing, He saith unto it only: Be! and it is.
Through him the Pen was set in motion. Upholding all things by the word of his power.
The Spirit proclaims before him. The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord.
“They regard Me according to what is with them and not according to what is with Me.” My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways.
“The pebbles glorify God in this luminous, white hand.” The stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it.
He has appeared “in such wise as to dazzle eyes”. His countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength; and when I saw him, I fell at his feet as dead.
What has appeared now never appeared before. Many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them.
Concealed in God’s knowledge until the appointed hour. The mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest.
The Promised One calls aloud, “yet most of the people perceive not”. He came unto his own, and his own received him not.
“The Quickener of bones.” I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live.
“Thy Lord is not prevented by anything.” The Qur’an’s name for God: Doer of what He will.
“Why and wherefore do not apply to His ways.” Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus? Hath not the potter power over the clay?

Abraham does ask why: wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked? Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right? And he is not rebuked for asking. Is there a questioning that the reading’s “He doeth whatsoever He willeth” leaves room for?

Socrates asks whether the holy is loved by the gods because it is holy, or holy because it is loved. If whatever He wills is right because He wills it, the second answer has been chosen. What follows for the meaning of “good”?
Do you think to extinguish the Sun? The Qur’an: fain would they put out the light of God with their mouths, but God will perfect His light however much the disbelievers are averse.
“The shame I was made to bear hath uncovered the glory.” Who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame.

The priests at the cross: he saved others; himself he cannot save; let him now come down, and we will believe him. Power, for them, would be escape. What do the readings mean by a power that is shown in not escaping?
All necks were laid low before him. That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow.
In the castles of his captivity the Báb paid no heed to the uproar. At midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
He stood before the world’s rulers, and no might could silence him. Jesus to Pilate: thou couldest have no power at all against me, except it were given thee from above.
He spoke before princes and divines. Ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them.
“Without veil or concealment.” This thing was not done in a corner.
“Under chains and the sword, arose to conquer East and West.” Paul from prison: I suffer trouble, as an evil doer, even unto bonds; but the word of God is not bound.
In prison and in chains he withstood kings. The things which happened unto me have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel; my bonds are manifest in all the palace.

From prison he “gained victory” over two kings. Machiavelli: all armed prophets have conquered, and the unarmed ones have been destroyed. Count the readings’ evidence. What kind of victory is being claimed, and would he recognise it?
Stone walls do not a prison make, nor iron bars a cage; minds innocent and quiet take that for an hermitage.
It was years after his passing before they knew who he was. Their eyes were holden that they should not know him.
The combined will of emperors and philosophers could not stamp it out. If it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it.
The reading quotes this saying: all power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.

Dostoevsky’s Grand Inquisitor reproaches Christ for refusing miracle, mystery and authority, the only powers, he says, that can hold mankind. He speaks for everyone who thinks the power of these readings too weak to rule. Is he answered?
His benediction still shines on this world. Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.
“I will send thee … with such a power as to astonish.” Ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto the uttermost part of the earth.
“He is with whosoever” speaks forth this Name. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
He strengthens whom He wills. He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do.
What honour is greater than to be remembered by Him? I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands.

shortfall: Many of the readings are short proclamations in closely similar words (He hath appeared with sovereignty; yet most perceive not) or prayers of praise; a companion was given to each distinct claim and not to each.
